characters.description: Will's assistant, still dependent on the serum that keeps him alive and unnaturally strong, and increasingly aware of who manufactures it and what that gives them over him. Rigid, honest, and unhappy, he is at the point where the treatment starts to feel like a leash.
characters.name: Jericho Jones

characters.description: Evie's oldest friend, done with waiting for a life of her own. Raised by campaigners and always cast as the sensible one, she is looking for work that matters and for people who take her seriously, and she has begun spending time with a circle of political radicals who do.
characters.name: Mabel Rose

characters.description: Evie's uncle, keeper of the museum and of a great deal he has never told her. He knows what the rising dead mean and he knows his own part in bringing the situation about, and he keeps choosing, day by day, not to say so.
characters.name: Will Fitzgerald

characters.description: Will's former colleague, who ran the wartime Diviner programme alongside him and has spent the years since trying to keep track of the children it produced. Careful and unsentimental, she is readier than Will to tell the young people the truth.
characters.name: Sister Walker

characters.description: The blind singer who drained Isaiah Campbell nearly to death and has been living with it since. His real name is Guillaume Johnson, and he was himself a subject of the wartime programme: it took his sight and left him able to pull the gift out of other Diviners. He is trying to be useful to the family he damaged.
characters.name: Bill Johnson

characters.description: America's most famous inventor and industrialist, building an exhibition to show the country its scientific future. He funded the wartime programme that made the Diviners, denies in public that Diviners exist, and treats anything he cannot control as a problem of engineering.
characters.name: Jake Marlowe

characters.description: The figure in the tall stovepipe hat who has been at the edges of the Diviners' dreams since the beginning: courteous, amused, attended by crows, and able to reach the dead and set them walking. He does not force anyone. He offers bargains and waits for people to accept them.
characters.name: The King of Crows

characters.description: A small boy shut up in the asylum on Ward's Island because of the visions he cannot stop having. He sees what is coming rather than what is, which has made him useless to his keepers and frightening to everyone else, and he recognises the Diviners for what they are as soon as he meets them.
characters.name: Conor Flynn

characters.description: An elderly resident of the Bennington who lays salt at the thresholds and is written off by her neighbours as senile. She is neither: she knows what walks at night, she has fought it before, and she has been waiting a very long time for someone to ask her about it.
characters.name: Adelaide Proctor

recaps.ending: Marlowe goes ahead with the Eye at his exhibition of the American future, and the breach it opens is far worse than he promised: the dead come through in force and the King of Crows is strengthened by it. The Diviners put their gifts together and force the tear shut, but the night ends in disaster. Mabel Rose is killed, and Marlowe and the newspapers hand the blame for the deaths to the Diviners, naming them anarchists and murderers rather than admit what his machine did. Will finally tells the whole truth about Project Buffalo: that he, Sister Walker, Marlowe and the colleague he loved dosed pregnant women during the war to manufacture Diviners, that the young people around him are its children, and that the door they opened at Hopeful Harbor was never properly closed. Sister Walker's warnings are vindicated far too late. Theta's reckoning with Roy leaves her unable to pretend the fire is under control. Jericho's dependence on Marlowe's serum has become a hold Marlowe can pull. Sam is left with what he learned about his mother and no way to act on it. With the law, the press and Marlowe's money against them, the group scatters and runs, hunted, grieving, and carrying the knowledge that the King of Crows is raising the dead across the whole country and that stopping him will mean leaving New York behind.
recaps.in_short: New York, autumn 1927. Evie's radio fame is fading when a visit to the asylum on Ward's Island puts the Diviners in front of the restless dead, who are no longer only ghosts: they rise, they attack, and they are being called by the man in the stovepipe hat, the King of Crows. Following the dead back to their source, the group finally learns the whole of Project Buffalo, the wartime programme run by Will Fitzgerald, Sister Walker and Jake Marlowe that dosed pregnant women to manufacture Diviners and tore something open at the estate called Hopeful Harbor. The Diviners are its children. While Marlowe prepares to demonstrate the Eye, a machine that draws power through that same breach, Mabel is drawn into a radical circle, Theta's violent husband finds her, and Bill Johnson's own part in the programme comes out. At Marlowe's exhibition the Eye tears the breach wide open, the dead pour through, and the Diviners close it at terrible cost: Mabel is killed, Will confesses everything, and Marlowe pins the deaths on the Diviners, who scatter and go on the run as wanted criminals.

recaps.text: Previously: Evie O'Neill, sent to New York in 1926 and able to read the past of any object she holds, helped destroy the spirit of the cult leader John Hobbes and became a national celebrity as a Diviner. The following winter, the dream walkers Ling Chan and Henry DuBois traced a sleeping sickness in Chinatown to the ghost of a woman who died in a collapsed tunnel beneath the city, and the group burned her remains to end it. Around Evie has gathered a circle of the gifted: Sam Lloyd, who can keep from being seen and whose mother was taken by government men; Theta Knight, who can call fire and fled an abusive husband in Kansas; her friend Henry; the Harlem healer Memphis Campbell and his brother Isaiah, whose visions are growing; Ling; Evie's friend Mabel Rose; and Will's assistant Jericho, kept alive by a serum from a wartime experiment. That experiment has a name, Project Buffalo, run during the war by Evie's uncle Will Fitzgerald, Sister Walker and the industrialist Jake Marlowe, and it is why so many young Diviners exist at once. Bill Johnson, an old blind man who steals power from Diviners, drained Isaiah into a coma before the boy was brought back. A figure in a stovepipe hat, attended by crows, has been waiting at the edges of their dreams, and beyond New York the dead have begun to rise.

Autumn 1927. Evie's radio programme is losing its shine and her sponsors are restless, so she agrees to a piece of publicity at the asylum on Ward's Island, reading objects for the newspapers among the forgotten patients there. The island turns out to be crowded with the dead, and they are not the quiet kind. Something on the island is awake and aware of the Diviners as soon as they arrive. Ling and Henry are now part of the group, Sam and Evie are circling each other, Memphis and Theta are still hiding their relationship, and Mabel is quietly tired of being the reliable one. Back at the Bennington, an old woman who lays salt across the thresholds tries to tell anyone who will listen that the dead are moving.

The dead on the island are not ordinary ghosts. They rise in numbers, they can injure and kill, and they are hungry in a way nobody can explain. In the wards the Diviners meet Conor Flynn, a small boy locked up for visions that turn out to be accurate, who warns them about what is coming. Evie's ability to read objects becomes an investigative tool: the dead leave traces, and the traces lead back toward a government programme and an estate outside the city. Theta's control over her fire slips under stress, and worse, the husband she ran from in Kansas turns up in New York looking for her. Bill Johnson, still living with what he did to Isaiah, begins to be useful, and the group learns his real name and that he was a subject of an experiment himself.

Project Buffalo is laid out in full. During the war the government dosed pregnant women and soldiers with a serum meant to produce Diviners, and the young people in the group are its children: their gifts were manufactured. The work was run by Will Fitzgerald, Sister Walker and Jake Marlowe at an estate called Hopeful Harbor, where a machine was used to reach into somewhere else, and where something came back through and was never properly shut out. Will has known all of this since before Evie came to live with him. The revelation splits the group's trust in the adults around them, and it explains why the Shadow Men have been following them for two years.

The man in the stovepipe hat stops waiting at the edges and presents himself: the King of Crows, courteous, entertained, and attended by crows, who can call the dead up out of the ground and set them walking. He does not compel anyone; he offers bargains, and he is patient about them. Reports of the dead rising arrive from beyond New York. Mabel, taken seriously at last by a circle of political radicals, commits herself to their work. Sam's search for his mother finally turns up something real, and the Shadow Men move to keep him from following it.

Jake Marlowe's exhibition of the American future takes shape around its centrepiece, the Eye: a machine that draws power from the same somewhere else the Hopeful Harbor experiment opened. Marlowe presents it as the end of scarcity and refuses to hear that it is a door. Jericho, whose serum comes from Marlowe's laboratories, takes more of it than he should and it changes him, making him stronger, quicker to anger, and easier to lead. Ling and Henry use dream walking to see what cannot be reached awake, and the Diviners work out that the King of Crows needs the breach open and that Marlowe is going to open it for him.

Adelaide Proctor finally tells her story: as a young woman she loved a man the King of Crows turned into something that would not stay dead, and she and her sister found a way to bind him. What she knows about salt, thresholds and binding gives the Diviners a way to fight the dead rather than only run from them, and they begin clearing hauntings across the city. Mabel's circle settles on direct action against Marlowe and his exhibition, and she does not tell Evie what she has agreed to. Theta's husband forces a confrontation she has spent three years avoiding.

With the exhibition days away and Marlowe unmoved by anything the Diviners say, the group prepares to stop the Eye themselves. Evie's public standing collapses as the newspapers turn on her, which frees her to act and leaves her without protection. Every strand converges on the exhibition grounds: Marlowe's demonstration, Mabel's radicals, the Shadow Men, the dead the King of Crows has been gathering, and the Diviners themselves, who now understand exactly what was done to them and by whom.

Marlowe switches on the Eye in front of the country and tears the breach wide open. The dead come through in force, the King of Crows is strengthened by it, and the Diviners join their gifts together to force the tear shut. They succeed, and the night is still a catastrophe: Mabel Rose is killed, and Marlowe and the press blame the deaths on the Diviners rather than on the machine, naming them anarchists and murderers. Will finally confesses the whole of Project Buffalo, that he, Sister Walker, Marlowe and the colleague he loved dosed pregnant women to manufacture Diviners, that the young people in front of him are the result, and that the door opened at Hopeful Harbor was never closed. Theta cannot pretend her fire is controllable any longer. Jericho's dependence on Marlowe's serum has become a leash. With the law, the newspapers and Marlowe's money against them, the group scatters and runs, grieving and hunted, knowing the King of Crows is raising the dead across the whole country and that whatever ends him is not in New York.

characters.description: The Northman warrior now travels west with Bayaz's company, far from his own country, one uneasy member of a fractious band bound for the edge of the World. Away from the constant fighting of his old life he tries again to be a better man, and finds a wary tenderness with the equally guarded Ferro. But the thing that lives in him when the killing starts - the Bloody-Nine, the reason the North both reveres and fears his name - is never as far below the surface as he wishes, and the hard road they travel offers plenty of chances for it to wake.
characters.name: Logen Ninefingers

characters.description: The crippled Inquisitor is sent far from Adua to the besieged Union city of Dagoska, clinging to the southern edge of the Gurkish Empire, to discover what became of his vanished predecessor and to hold the city against an overwhelming army. Racked with pain and short of everything but enemies, Glokta plays the city's merchants, mercenaries, and native townsfolk against one another, forever aware that the debts he is running up may be called in by patrons more frightening than the Gurkish. His mordant wit and his refusal to simply lie down remain his only real weapons.
characters.name: Sand dan Glokta

characters.description: The vain young officer, so pleased with himself at home, is dragged along on Bayaz's grueling journey through a ruined and war-torn land, stripped of the comforts and admiration he took for granted. Cold, hungry, frightened, and often useless, Jezal is forced for the first time to measure himself against real hardship and against companions who care nothing for his rank. Slowly, and painfully, the shallow young man begins to change, and he finds himself drawn to the fierce and unwelcoming Ferro.
characters.name: Jezal dan Luthar

characters.description: Still burning for revenge on the Gurkish who enslaved her, Ferro travels west with Bayaz, told that the weapon they seek may be the tool of the vengeance she craves. Suspicious of every kindness and braced always for betrayal, she is unsettled to find the Northman Logen refusing to give up on her, and more unsettled by the strangeness Bayaz keeps hinting at in her own blood. She does not trust the wizard's purposes, but his road runs toward her enemies, so she follows it.
characters.name: Ferro Maljinn

characters.description: The First of the Magi leads his company across the desolate Old Empire toward the ruined city at the edge of the World, hunting an ancient thing he calls the Seed - a relic of a war among his own kind ages past, which he means to turn against the Gurkish prophet Khalul. Impatient and secretive, Bayaz doles out his history and his reasons a fragment at a time, and the flashes of raw power he shows when pressed make plain that the legends about the Magi are not entirely stories. What he actually intends, and what it will cost the people following him, he keeps to himself.
characters.name: Bayaz

characters.description: Promoted and posted to the North, West serves on the staff of Crown Prince Ladisla's army in the war against King Bethod - a campaign hamstrung by the vanity and incompetence of its royal commander. A capable, conscientious man watching fools throw away lives, West struggles to keep his temper in check as disaster looms, and when the army meets catastrophe he is thrown together with a band of hard Northern scouts and must find his own steel to survive the wilderness.
characters.name: Collem West

characters.description: Having given up the search for Logen, the Dogman and the survivors of his old crew - Threetrees, Tul Duru, Grim, and Black Dow - throw in with the Union's northern army, offering their skills as scouts against Bethod, whom they hate as much as any Union man does. Wry and watchful as ever, the Dogman finds himself increasingly relied upon as the campaign unravels, and forms an unlikely bond with the Union officer West when the two are cast together in the wreckage.
characters.name: The Dogman

characters.description: A famous and infamous soldier of fortune, Nicomo Cosca commands a mercenary company hired into the defence of Dagoska. Flamboyant, unreliable, and usually drunk, he treats war as a business and loyalty as a matter of the current price, which makes him both useful and profoundly dangerous to Glokta, who must decide how far a man like this can be trusted when the coin runs short and the walls are breached. Beneath the theatrics is a shrewd and surprisingly resilient operator.
characters.name: Nicomo Cosca

characters.description: The Crown Prince of the Union, heir to the throne and nominal commander of the army sent north against Bethod. Ladisla is a preening, foppish young man with grand notions of martial glory and no capacity whatsoever to lead, surrounded by flatterers and contemptuous of the professional soldiers, like West, who actually understand the war. His hunger for a heroic victory, untempered by any sense, steers the northern campaign toward calamity.
characters.name: Crown Prince Ladisla

recaps.ending: Before They Are Hanged ends with all three campaigns in ruins. Bayaz's company reaches the island at the edge of the World only to find the Seed beyond their reach; the quest that justified everything fails outright, and the magus's ruthless, ancient nature is now plain to those who travelled with him. Jezal returns disfigured and humbled, bound uneasily to Ferro. In the South, Dagoska falls to the Gurkish and Glokta escapes with his life, carrying the knowledge that the banking house Valint and Balk owns the Union's debts - and, through blackmail, owns him. In the North, Prince Ladisla's army has been destroyed; Collem West has survived only by joining the Dogman's crew, but at the cost of beating the prince to death after Ladisla tried to rape the woman Cathil, a killing he must now conceal. Rudd Threetrees is dead and the Dogman leads what remains of the old crew. Every party turns back toward Adua: the quest empty-handed, a city lost, a royal army wiped out, and a prince secretly murdered. The Union is weaker, its enemies bolder, and Bayaz's true purpose - and the price of it - still hidden as the final book opens.
recaps.in_short: The three roads opened at the end of the first book run to bitter ends. Bayaz leads Logen, Jezal, Ferro and the rest west across the ruined Old Empire to the edge of the World in search of the Seed, enduring pursuit and starvation; Jezal is humbled and scarred and grows closer to Ferro, but the quest fails and the weapon is never recovered, while the darker truth of the magus becomes harder to deny. In the South, Glokta struggles to hold Dagoska against the Gurkish with threats, bribes and Cosca's mercenaries, uncovers treachery within, and learns that a hidden banking house, Valint and Balk, secretly controls the Union and now controls him; Dagoska falls and he barely escapes. In the North, Prince Ladisla's army is annihilated, and West, cast into the wilderness with the Dogman's crew, beats the cowardly prince to death after Ladisla attacks a woman under their protection. Threetrees is killed and the Dogman becomes chief. Battered and empty-handed, all of them turn back toward Adua and a Union sliding toward collapse.

recaps.text: Previously, in The Blade Itself: Bayaz, First of the Magi - an old wizard most people believed to be a myth - forced his way onto the Union's ruling Closed Council and gathered an unlikely company. The Northman Logen Ninefingers, the crippled and bitter Inquisitor Glokta, the vain young Contest champion Jezal dan Luthar, and the vengeful escaped Gurkish slave Ferro Maljinn were each drawn, willing or not, into his orbit, along with the apprentice Malacus Quai and the Navigator Brother Longfoot. Bayaz revealed his purpose: a journey west, past the edge of the known World, to recover the Seed - an ancient weapon out of the Old Time that he insists is the only thing that can stop the Gurkish Empire and its Prophet, Khalul. As the Union braced for war with King Bethod in the North and the threat of the Gurkish in the South, the company set out. Arch Lector Sult sent Glokta south to take command of the isolated fortress-city of Dagoska, whose previous Superior had vanished. Major Collem West marched north with the Union army under the vain, foolish Crown Prince Ladisla, entrusting his sister Ardee to Glokta before he left. Three roads opened - a quest, a siege, and a war - with Bayaz alone knowing where each truly led.

The three roads run apart across the map. Bayaz's company grinds westward into the Old Empire, once the heart of civilization and now a lawless waste of feuding warlords and ruined cities, and the travellers learn quickly that the magus's road offers neither comfort nor safety and that he will explain almost nothing. Logen and Ferro circle each other warily; Jezal, soft and self-pitying, is worn down by hardship he has never known. In the far South, Glokta reaches Dagoska to find the city rotting from within: his predecessor gone without trace, the Gurkish army massing beyond the walls, the ruling merchants led by Magister Eider pursuing their own ends, and the native townsfolk kept as second-class subjects behind the walls. He sets about shoring up the crumbling defences by any ruthless means available. In the North, West serves in Crown Prince Ladisla's army as it advances against Bethod, and watches royal vanity, jealousy and sheer incompetence steer a large force toward disaster against a canny and patient enemy who knows the ground far better than they do.

Each strand tightens toward crisis. In Dagoska, Glokta holds the city together with threats, bribery and the unreliable mercenary company of Nicomo Cosca, all the while hunting the traitor feeding the Gurkish from inside the walls; his search leads toward Magister Eider and the merchants, and he begins to sense a hidden power - a banking house - moving behind the Union's affairs. Out in the Old Empire, Bayaz's party endures pursuit, starvation and the magus's maddening secrecy as it presses toward the coast; Jezal, stripped of his vanity by suffering, slowly becomes a better man and grows closer to Ferro. In the North, Prince Ladisla's army marches straight into catastrophe: it is ambushed and shattered at a river crossing, and West is flung into the wilderness with a handful of survivors, thrown together with the Dogman and the last of Logen's old crew - Threetrees, Tul Duru, Black Dow and Grim - and with a hard-bitten woman, Cathil, rescued from a labour camp. What began as three orderly campaigns has collapsed into three desperate fights simply to stay alive.

Every strand reaches a bitter turn. Bayaz's company at last crosses the Old Empire - passing through the dead city of Aulcus, where they are attacked and Jezal's face is smashed and scarred - and reaches the island at the very edge of the World where the Seed should lie. There the quest fails: the ancient weapon is beyond their grasp, the whole terrible journey seemingly for nothing, and the glimpses of what Bayaz truly is, and what he did in ages past, grow impossible to ignore. Dagoska falls to the Gurkish; Glokta escapes the city's ruin having confirmed that a shadowy banking house, Valint and Balk, secretly holds the Union - and now holds him. In the North, the scattered survivors of Ladisla's army fight their way back through the wilderness; Rudd Threetrees, the old crew's leader, is killed, and the Dogman takes his place. Crown Prince Ladisla, cowardly and cruel to the end, attempts to force himself on Cathil, and West, in a fury, beats him to death - a desperate, irreversible act that will shadow everything after. Bloodied and changed, all three parties turn at last back toward Adua: the quest empty-handed, the South lost, the North in ruins. Nothing Bayaz promised has come to pass, and the Union is weaker and more exposed than when the book began.

characters.description: A defeated bandit leader from the earlier conflict involving Fa Ram. His ambush killed people under Cai Xiulan's command, leaving her burdened by their deaths and by the public account of his defeat.
characters.name: Sun Ken

characters.description: The farmer and head of Fa Ram, newly married to Meiling. Jin is enlarging the farm, sharing its work among a growing household, and teaching Cai Xiulan while continuing to value useful labor over status.
characters.name: Jin

characters.description: Jin's wife, a healer and farmer who shares responsibility for Fa Ram's home, fields, and expanding household. Three weeks into their marriage, she works beside Jin and helps direct the farm's daily routines.
characters.name: Meiling

recaps.ending: Fa Ram begins its expanded harvest with Jin and the pregnant Meiling remaining at its center. Bi De has returned with Yin, Miantiao, and a damaged crystal that preserves fragments of an ancient land-empowering formation and its catastrophe. Jin supports a careful investigation, Cai Xiulan plans to seek relevant material in her sect library, and Miantiao accepts useful work and treatment at Fa Ram, although his spinal injuries remain. Tigu is healthy in human form but has found no way to become a cat again. Wa Shi can shift into a dragonlike form, and the rest of the household has gained new infrastructure, responsibilities, and family ties. Cai Xiulan, now in the Profound Realm, departs for the Dueling Peaks tournament with Tigu, Gou Ren, Ri Zu, and Yun Ren. Lu Ri's network has traced Jin Jue to Verdant Hill without confirming Jin's identity, while Lu Ban commands Fangtip Fortress from Zang Li's stolen body and retains a hidden cultivation scroll. The ancient wound in the Azure Hills and the attention gathering around Jin therefore remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Newly married, Jin and Meiling expand Fa Ram while Cai Xiulan struggles with guilt from the battle against Sun Ken. The household's care helps her recover and reach the Profound Realm. Bi De leaves to study scattered shrines, gains Yin and Miantiao as companions, and discovers that the Azure Hills contain a broken five-element formation. Wa Shi returns from hidden training able to take a dragonlike form, while Tigu survives a tribulation and becomes human. Meiling learns she is pregnant, heals a contamination crisis in Verdant Hill, and returns home. Lu Ri's search for Jin Jue reaches the region without exposing Jin, while Lu Ban remains concealed in Zang Li's stolen body. Bi De brings an ancient damaged crystal back to Fa Ram, and Jin agrees to help investigate it. At harvest, Cai Xiulan leads Tigu, Gou Ren, Ri Zu, and Yun Ren away toward the Dueling Peaks tournament, leaving Jin and Meiling with the growing household.

recaps.text: Previously: Jin Jue left the Cloudy Sword Sect after an inner disciple nearly killed him and became the farmer Jin in the Azure Hills. At Fa Ram he built a home centered on cultivation through land, food, and useful work. Meiling became his closest partner, and friends from Hong Yaowu joined a household that also includes awakened animals. Big D, also called Bi De, serves as Jin's first disciple and senior guardian. Tigu, Ri Zu, Chun Ke, Pi Pa, and Wa Shi have their own abilities and places within the farm. The household also bears scars from Chow Ji's corruption, including Bi De's lasting injuries and Ri Zu's knowledge of the methods used against them. Jin's refuge is therefore peaceful but not isolated from the consequences of earlier violence or his abandoned sect identity.

Jin and Meiling settle into married life while expanding Fa Ram's fields, livestock, and beehives. Cai Xiulan works beside Gou Ren and the animal disciples, searching for the cultivation lesson behind Jin's farming. Her rivalry with Tigu becomes a productive training partnership, and she senses a damaged earth spirit connected to the farm, although her forceful approach drives it away. Beneath her progress, nightmares from the battle against Sun Ken return. Cai Xiulan blames herself for the people who died under her leadership and struggles with the praise attached to the false public account of her victory. Jin and Meiling recognize her distress without pressing her. When she finally breaks down, Meiling stays with her through the night and helps her speak about the dead rather than carrying them alone. Meanwhile, Jin and Meiling deliver two healthy calves, complete the main spring planting, and organize the household's work. With the rice transplanted and the farm entering a quieter period, Jin, Meiling, Cai Xiulan, and Gou Ren leave for Hong Yaowu.

Jin's group is welcomed into Hong Yaowu while Pi Pa manages Fa Ram and Ri Zu oversees the calves. Cai Xiulan begins participating in village life and grows closer to Meiling's family. At a spiritually potent clearing, the damaged earth spirit corrects the rigid movement of her sword form, steering her toward a more natural dance. Back at Fa Ram, Tigu's contempt for Ri Zu's medicine leads Ri Zu to demonstrate that she can paralyze Tigu with controlled medicinal chi. Chun Ke persuades Tigu that both disciples have been trying to force respect and friendship. A cautious exchange of instruction and tea begins a truce between them. Cai Xiulan then tells Jin how the celebrated version of Sun Ken's defeat erases the dead and intensifies her guilt. Jin affirms her compassion and asks to be treated as a friend as well as a teacher. In her next nightmare, Cai Xiulan breaks the repeated sequence of defeat, uses the unfamiliar dance in her sword work, and overcomes the embodiment of her self-blame. She accepts that mourning those she led is not a weakness.

Wa Shi vanishes into a sealed watery realm, where an ancient black turtle identifies him as a young dragon and begins teaching him control of water. Elsewhere, Lu Ri traces Jin Jue's departure from the Cloudy Sword Sect. Sect leaders discover that Jin was nearly killed amid systematic abuse of outer disciples, punish the responsible inner disciple, and order Lu Ri to continue a discreet search toward the Azure Hills. At Fa Ram, Meiling takes charge of accounts while Jin cultivates unusual plants. Bi De becomes convinced that the scattered solstice sites must be studied directly, and Jin supports his wish to travel. In Verdant Hill, Jin arranges a trial sale of maple syrup, researches regional plants and animals, and gains approval for a road linking the town to Hong Yaowu. The magistrate also asks Bi De to address dangerous animals during his journey. Meiling stays behind to support Meihua through childbirth. After mapping visible formation points and obtaining a broader regional map, Bi De leaves the Shrine of Fire alone. His expedition now combines service to threatened settlements with a search for the purpose of the ancient sites.

Meiling identifies contaminated well water as the cause of illness in Verdant Hill and works with its magistrate and lady to contain the threat. Her medicinal chi clears the contamination, and she also heals the lady's long-standing injury. At Fa Ram, Wa Shi returns from the hidden realm able to shift between carp and dragonlike forms. A flight with him carries Cai Xiulan into the Profound Realm. Meihua safely gives birth to a son, and soon afterward Meiling tells Jin that she is pregnant. Bi De's travels lead him to Eighth Correct Place, where he kills the unnatural wolf called the Terror, aids the damaged village, and gives its defender Zheng Fei basic martial training. Farther on, he finds a village destroyed by Sun Ken and meets Yin, an awakened rabbit, and her crippled snake master Miantiao. Miantiao admits that he trained Yin as a weapon for revenge and planned to abandon her while seeking death. Bi De refuses to kill him and insists that atonement requires living differently. Yin secures Miantiao's promise to live, and both join Bi De's investigation of the regional shrines and dances.

Tigu asks Fa Ram's earth spirit for a human form so she can communicate and live among the household without the barriers of her cat body. Warned that the change may kill her, she accepts a lightning tribulation and survives as a human woman. Jin and Meiling affirm that she remains family, and Ri Zu finds her new body healthy rather than corrupted. Tigu cannot return to cat form, but repeated tests reveal no injury and suggest that her own wishes may anchor the transformation. Beyond Fa Ram, Lu Ban wins standing within the Shrouded Mountain Sect while occupying the body of the murdered Zang Li. He is posted north to Fangtip Fortress and intends to exploit the freedom it offers. Jin's own bond with his crops deepens, and Babe reveals that he has long been an awakened ox who freely chooses plowing as his work. During Bi De's expedition, repeated shrine layouts, altered elemental sites, and a vision in the Ash Forest reveal an immense five-element pattern across the Azure Hills. The ancient formation is damaged, its center is empty, and its original purpose remains unknown.

Lu Ri organizes the Plum Blossom's Shadow to search for Jin Jue and sends an agent to Verdant Hill. The magistrate blocks the covert inquiry and warns Jin without exposing his identity. Jin considers drawing future investigators away from Fa Ram. At home, he and Gou Ren complete a water-powered mill, while Tigu asks to accompany Cai Xiulan to the Dueling Peaks tournament. Jin tests her judgment through road work and difficult errands in Verdant Hill. She controls her temper and passes. Yun Ren's northern travels lead him through an illusion into a hidden tomb guarded by a giant white fox. Because he respects the grave and seeks a way to preserve images, the guardian teaches him an illusion technique and later recognizes him as a relative through his mother's bloodline. A nearby Shrouded Mountain force fails to find the refuge, while Lu Ban secretly takes a scroll called The Blade of Fire at Fangtip Fortress. Yun Ren leaves with new skill and an invitation for the guardian to meet his family. Jin and Meiling decide to remain home because of her pregnancy. Cai Xiulan, Tigu, Gou Ren, and Ri Zu form the expected tournament party, and Fa Ram adopts a shared emblem as several disciples consider family names.

Lu Ri reaches Fangtip Fortress and forces its Shrouded Mountain young master to confirm Jin's earlier presence in Verdant Hill. At the same time, Bi De, Yin, and Miantiao enter the last marked formation site. After a difficult descent through hostile caves, they find murals of an ancient human-and-beast society and recover a damaged crystal containing fragmented memories. The images show leaders empowering the land, followed by war, corruption, and catastrophe, but do not explain the cause. Bi De returns to Fa Ram with his companions and the crystal. Meiling removes a corruptive remnant from Miantiao, though she cannot repair his old spinal damage, and Jin offers him glassmaking work. Jin agrees to support a patient investigation of the formation, while Cai Xiulan offers to search her sect's library. Bi De chooses the name Fa Bi De to bind himself to his home. As the enlarged household begins harvesting, Cai Xiulan reflects on her recovery and her new place in the Profound Realm. Jin and Meiling remain at Fa Ram, expecting their child. Cai Xiulan accepts responsibility for Tigu, Gou Ren, and Ri Zu, then departs with them and Yun Ren toward the Dueling Peaks tournament.

recaps.ending: The Shrouded Mountain assault is settled through reparations, rebuilding, and withdrawal rather than further retaliation. Lu Ban is confirmed dead, though an unidentified infiltrator preserves a trace of his grudge for possible future harm. Cai Xiulan's internal injury is healed, but her cultivation remains reduced and she chooses to rebuild on gentler terms. Tigu accepts both her human and tiger forms, and her bonds with Ri Zu, Loud Boy, Rags, and the Hermetic Iron young master widen Fa Ram's circle. Loud Boy and Rags leave to seek restoration of his cultivation, while Liu Bowu travels to Fa Ram for treatment. Jin refuses a return to the Cloudy Sword Sect but retains Gramps' letter, gift, and favor. He and Meiling await their child and accept that Fa Ram is now known to powerful outsiders. The ancient recording, the earth spirit's damaged past, the politically sensitive Dueling Peaks archive, and a possible southern trading expedition remain open. Liu Xianghua formally asks Gou Ren's parents for permission to court him.
recaps.in_short: Jin takes Fa Ram's extraordinary harvest to market while Tigu, Cai Xiulan, and their companions attend the Dueling Peaks tournament. The journey uncovers Jin's commercial importance, a message from Gramps, and an ancient crystal record linked to broken formations. Cai Xiulan wins the tournament over Tigu, but Lu Ban and the Shrouded Mountain Sect abduct Tigu and attack her allies. The Azure Hills cultivators unite in resistance, Jin defeats Lu Ban, and he prevents a wider war by demanding compensation and reconstruction. Cai Xiulan survives severe cultivation damage and receives further healing from Fa Ram's earth spirit. The household returns home intact but newly exposed to provincial politics. Jin refuses to rejoin the Cloudy Sword Sect, Tigu forms new friendships, and Liu Xianghua begins openly courting Gou Ren. Lu Ban is dead, yet an unknown woman retains a residue of his grudge, while the ancient formation, the Dueling Peaks archive, and Fa Ram's broader responsibilities remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Jin established Fa Ram as a home shared with Meiling and a growing household of awakened animals and human companions. He is also known as Jin Jue, a name tied to an earlier life in cultivation. Meiling developed her work as a healer, while Jin's disciples learned to cultivate, protect one another, and take on responsibilities of their own. Cai Xiulan survived grave wounds and demonic chi after the conflict with Sun Ken because Jin and Meiling treated her. That recovery deepened her connection to their household. Jin also came into conflict with a powerful Shrouded Mountain figure while protecting Meihua, leaving a dangerous grievance unresolved. By the start of this volume, Fa Ram is prosperous and closely bonded, but its unusual people, products, and strength are becoming harder to keep beyond the notice of sects and merchants.

Jin's unusually early rice harvest is too valuable for the market in Verdant Hill, so he plans to sell it in Pale Moon Lake City and seek help for a deteriorating crystal. Meiling remains at Fa Ram to continue her medical work. Cai Xiulan, Tigu, Ri Zu, Gou Ren, and Yun Ren reach the city on their way to the Dueling Peaks. A crystal carver cannot restore the damaged object but offers access to a more senior expert. At the tournament town, Cai Xiulan secures her sect's welcome for Jin's household, while Tigu registers as the group's only competitor. Gou Ren meets Liu Xianghua, the Misty Lake young mistress who considers Cai Xiulan a rival. Jin sets out with Bi De, Yin, and Miantiao, carrying three hundred bags of rice and seeking both supplies and information about people looking for him. Meanwhile Lu Ri follows signs of Jin Jue, and Lu Ban arrives to scout tournament talent for the Shrouded Mountain Sect.

The Dueling Peaks tournament opens with Cai Xiulan publicly confirmed in the Profound Realm and Tigu measured as a powerful Initiate. Both advance through the preliminary round, and Tigu earns respect by using a one-sided match to teach her opponent. She and Ri Zu then explore the Hill of Torment, where Tigu kills a dangerous five-venom spider. Jin reaches Pale Moon Lake City and learns that repairing the ancient crystal could take decades. A possible transfer into another high-quality crystal instead sends him toward an elderly holder near the tournament. His harvest proves equally consequential: the Azure Jade Trading Company identifies the rice as gold-grade, agrees to buy his large supply, and purchases Fa Ram's maple syrup at a premium. Jin preserves his original merchant relationship and uses the new agreement to seek medical learning for Meiling, whose pregnancy he confirms.

Jin acquires industrial materials, medical references, and plans for equipment through the Azure Jade Trading Company. He also considers a difficult southern search for cacao and coffee. At Fa Ram, Meiling manages the farm while a damaged earth spirit appears in her dreams, revealing broken dragon veins and painful missing memories. Cloudy Sword agents trace Jin's altered city identity to Jin Jue and request a meeting. Though afraid of his former sect, Jin accepts support from Bi De, Yin, and Miantiao rather than facing Lu Ri alone. Lu Ri approaches with courtesy and delivers a sealed letter from Gramps. The message confirms that Jin's adoptive grandfather is alive but away on an undisclosed duty, and that he has left a gift which will open when Jin reaches a later stage. Lu Ri also conveys the Cloudy Sword Sect's apology, an offer of reinstatement, reparations, and protection. Jin must now decide whether any return to the sect has a place in the life he built at Fa Ram.

A recollection shows how the orphaned Jin Jue was rescued and trained by Gramps before being sent to the Cloudy Sword Sect. In the present, Joe and Jin Jue reconcile as the two conscious remnants within Jin's shared existence. They choose Fa Ram and its people over a return to sect life. Jin refuses reinstatement, receives Gramps' sword and sealed scroll, and accepts the sect's sincere amends on his own terms. At the tournament, Tigu survives Liu Xianghua's steam-powered furnace and wins their hard contest. Their respect grows, while Xianghua's showing improves the standing of her mechanically gifted younger brother, Liu Bowu. Tigu later defeats the Hermetic Iron young master, and Cai Xiulan defeats the Grand Ravine finalist, setting a final between the two women. A broad celebration brings rival sect disciples together. Cai Xiulan senses an incomplete five-part harmony in their shared dance, strengthening her hope that relationships across sect boundaries can serve more than competition.

Jin's group reaches the hidden monkey settlement at Crystal Hill. The clan leader agrees to transfer the damaged recording into a preserved crystal in exchange for knowledge of the clan's former master. Matching spiral designs connect the settlement to Bi De's wider formation inquiry. The group chooses a fast, irreversible procedure powered largely by Jin. At the Dueling Peaks, Cai Xiulan and Tigu prepare for their final while Ri Zu begins treatment that lets Liu Bowu take steps without a crutch. Lu Ban studies Tigu's recorded fights and connects her master to Jin, turning his attention toward the household. The crystal ritual becomes unstable after detecting something alive within the recording and pulls Jin, his disciples, and the monkeys into its memories. Bi De links their separate memory prisons while Yin, Miantiao, and the monkey leader fight corrupt shades. They rescue the full group and encounter the remnant of an ancient guardian. Everyone returns alive, and the transfer succeeds, but Jin is severely depleted and the catastrophe preserved in the crystal remains unexplained.

Cai Xiulan defeats Tigu in the tournament final, and the two openly affirm their bond afterward. The celebration ends when a Shrouded Mountain visitor seeks to recruit Cai Xiulan and probes for Jin and Tigu. His followers then abduct Tigu, gravely wound Rags, and destroy Loud Boy's cultivation. Cai Xiulan and Ri Zu begin a desperate rescue, while attacks spread to Gou Ren and Yun Ren. Ri Zu frees Tigu by helping her use the cat form she had feared, and Azure Hills competitors from rival sects unite against the attackers. Yun Ren becomes the eighth wielder of the sentient sword Summer's Sky, and Bi De arrives in time to protect a badly burned Cai Xiulan. Jin enters the fighting, rescues Yun Ren, and confronts the sect force. He accepts a temporary de-escalation to prevent immediate war, then faces Lu Ban, the hostile figure behind the assault. Jin overwhelms Lu Ban's defenses with one earth-empowered strike, ending the attack, although Lu Ban's survival and the political consequences are still uncertain.

Ri Zu stabilizes the wounded, but Cai Xiulan's fire injury threatens her ability to cultivate. Evidence from Lu Ban's remains convinces the Shrouded Mountain contingent that its supposed young master was corrupted or replaced. Jin requires medicine, resources, and cooperation while allowing an investigation. Elsewhere, a mortal maintenance worker awakens an ancient Dueling Peaks system and leads the local elders into a hidden archive before a damaged defense mechanism traps them. The elders eventually disable the barrier and secure the archive as politically neutral ground. In town, Jin turns the aftermath toward restitution. Fighters from every faction rebuild homes and streets, while he compensates a blacksmith for his own collateral damage. Tigu confirms she can still take tiger form and begins to reconsider revenge after speaking with Bi De. Cai Xiulan survives with greatly reduced cultivation, accepts Jin as sworn family, and resolves to rebuild on a kinder path. Jin then negotiates a settlement requiring reconstruction and compensation for the mortal dead while protecting those who came to Tigu's aid.

The Shrouded Mountain Sect discovers that its original disciple had been dead for about a year and that an ancient body-eater occupied his body. The sect accepts Jin's limited terms, sends substantial reparations, agrees not to enter the Azure Hills without his permission, and withdraws its surviving disciples. Jin distributes resources to the town and the injured, directing future emergencies through the Azure Jade Trading Company. Fa Ram's golden earth spirit reveals that its links helped the household endure the assault. Its healing dance repairs Cai Xiulan's internal damage, though her cultivation remains diminished and the spirit is distressed by recovered memories of ancient exploitation. Jin leaves provincial authority with a simple instruction to protect people and chooses to return home. Tigu exchanges gifts with the Hermetic Iron young master and invites him to visit. She also becomes sworn siblings with Loud Boy and Rags. The two independent fighters leave to seek restoration of Loud Boy's cultivation, aided by the breakthrough pills Cai Xiulan won at the tournament. Jin's party departs with Liu Bowu and a monkey.

Jin's party returns to Fa Ram. Meiling has developed a promising method that uses Wa Shi's lightning to strengthen spiritual-herb preparations, and she believes Liu Bowu's damaged knee can be treated. Jin struggles with delayed distress after the violence and unwanted political authority, but work, family, and shared plans help him recover his balance. He accepts that Fa Ram cannot return to anonymity and decides to seek governance advice, study Gramps' scroll, and let the household face future duties together. The disciples likewise recognize that Jin's strength alone cannot protect a home now known to outside powers. A visit to Bi De's disciple reveals Zheng Fei defending his village with a rooster mask, spear, dog, and warning talisman. In the closing developments, Liu Xianghua formally asks Gou Ren's parents for permission to court him. Lu Ban is confirmed dead, but an unidentified woman infiltrates Shrouded Mountain storage and takes a small residue of his grudge for possible revenge. Lu Ri's mission report reaches the Cloudy Sword elders, leaving Jin's refusal to return in place without creating a new conflict.
